boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fort McAllister II record (December 13, 1864) in the Savannah Campaign [November-December 1864]. The investment of Savannah (December 10-21) and the evacuation of the city are outside the record. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads the 2nd Division, XV Corps against the Fort McAllister garrison (120 men); the live field reads zeros. Hazen says his division had an effective strength of 4,426 on November 15 and that nine regiments were deployed for the assault; he gives the garrison, including killed, as 250. Cox says three regiments from each of the three brigades assaulted and puts the garrison at about 200 under Major G. W. Anderson.
claims.rationale: Hazen's 4,426 is a division strength a month earlier; the garrison figures (120, about 200, 250 including killed) differ in source and basis. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.rationale: The fort and its obstacles predate the assault. Narrative descriptions.

claims.value: NPS says Sherman ordered Howard to take the fort and Howard chose Hazen. Cox says Hazen delayed the attack to use portions of each of his three brigades, over Colonel W. S. Jones's wish to attack at once, and that there was no formal surrender. Hazen says Martin took command of the Second Brigade when its commander fell. The frozen commanders are Brigadier General Hazen (US) and Major George A. Anderson (CS); Cox names 'Major G. W. Anderson'.
claims.rationale: Direction is attributed as the sources state; Cox's initials for Anderson are not adopted. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 205 (US 134; CS 71); the live field reads 384 (US 134; CS 250). Hazen and Cox both give Hazen's loss as 24 killed and 110 wounded. Hazen gives the captured garrison, including killed, as 250; Cox gives the garrison's loss as 48.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Hazen's 250 counts the whole garrison captured or killed, not casualties.

open_questions: Howard's No. 7, Osterhaus's No. 11 and the brigade reports (Nos. 22–29), Sherman's No. 1 report and Special Field Orders No. 131 (read, not selected), Anderson's and other Confederate accounts, and the Navy reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. C. R. Woods's, G. W. Smith's, Kilpatrick's, Wheeler's, J. P. Hatch's and Hazen's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLIV, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Jacob D. Cox's The March to the Sea; Franklin and Nashville (1882) is a later history drawing on the official papers; Cox was not in this campaign. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
